toegepas.voor: oud en het haar eerste niggie gekry
toegepas.na: oud, en dit was haar eerste niggie
toegepas.rede_vinder: Avoids repeating 'gekry' from the sentence before, where it means the parents had a baby, and keeps the meaning that this is Mila's first niece.
toegepas.fout: 'gekry' is repeated straight after the previous sentence in a different sense (the parents had a baby, Mila got a niece), which reads clumsily.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The proposal removes the jarring repetition, keeps the same fact (the baby is Mila's first niece), and correctly adds the AWS comma between two full clauses.

toegepas.rede_vinder: The fixed Afrikaans expression is 'die een na die ander'.
toegepas.fout: The fixed expression is incomplete without its article.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'die een na die ander' is the standard fixed Afrikaans expression and the meaning is unchanged.

toegepas.voor: Zanele het haar intussen die woorde van die lied geleer
toegepas.na: Intussen het Zanele vir Mila die woorde van die lied geleer
toegepas.rede_vinder: With Zanele as subject, 'haar' can be read as Zanele herself; naming Mila removes the ambiguity.
toegepas.fout: With Zanele as subject, 'haar' can be read reflexively, and 'geleer' can mean learn as well as teach, so the sentence could mean Zanele learned the words herself.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Naming Mila with 'vir Mila' removes the ambiguity without adding information, since the same people, action and time remain.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A future seen from the past takes 'sou' in a past-tense narrative, matching 'die naam sou kies' in the previous sentence.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Gaan stry' with 'vandag' reads naturally as Mila's own fear in the story, and 'sou stry' adds a conditional colour while making the narrator's voice stiffer.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Lifting and holding a baby up is 'hoog ophou'; 'hoog hou' is unidiomatic here.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Die baba hoog gehou' is natural Afrikaans, and 'opgehou' could make a Grade 6 reader stumble on 'ophou' meaning 'stop'.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Bekommerd voel' echoes English 'felt worried'; 'was bekommerd' is the natural Afrikaans.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Bekommerd gevoel' is ordinary, natural Afrikaans rather than an anglicism, so swapping it is a lateral move in the author's voice.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: Mila het dit nog altyd geweet
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'Nog altyd' is the Afrikaans for 'had always known' up to that moment; bare 'altyd' reads as habitual.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Mila het dit altyd geweet' already reads well against 'Vandag' that follows, so 'nog altyd' is only a different way of saying it in the story.
